notes: Switzerland Hardening I–III M2.5 reviews preserved (42/42). Hardening IV M2.5 human semantic review for CC-CH-REG-001..017 (monetary / FX regime / exchange-control). Classification only: not adopted; no claims.json / field_bindings / adoption_decision / switzerland.json writes; no Passage Check posture selected. Doctrine: de jure free floating ≠ de facto crawl-like; crawl-like ≠ crawling peg/managed-float invention; SNB intervention ≠ exchange control; Article VIII current international transactions ≠ capital account; IMF security exception preserved; OECD reservations remain actor/transaction-specific; no 'freely convertible' / 'no capital controls' / 'fully liberalised' manufactured. Total ledger 59/59.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Unrestricted amounts of cash, i.e. notes and coins, foreign currencies and bearer negotiable instruments (shares, bonds and cheques) may be carried into, through and out of Switzerland.
reviews.rationale: FOCBS verbatim carriage-quantity proposition is supported for notes and coins, foreign currencies and bearer negotiable instruments (shares, bonds and cheques) into, through and out of Switzerland. Scope is quantitative carriage amount only. Does not establish absence of information-on-request, AML/TF suspicion powers, sanctions, seizure, banking restrictions, or capital-account rules.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Cash carried into, through or out of Switzerland is not obliged to be declared to the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS).
reviews.reviewed_text: Notes and coins, foreign currencies and bearer negotiable instruments (shares, bonds and cheques) carried into, through or out of Switzerland are not obliged to be declared to the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS).
reviews.rationale: Bounded to restore the FOCBS antecedent instrument categories into the no-declaration proposition and to keep the stronger 'not obliged to declare' wording (not weakened to 'normal amounts'). Negative claim is limited to spontaneous FOCBS declaration within the cross-border cash framework. Does not establish absence of questioning, recording, seizure, AML/TF rules, or other controls.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: If a person is questioned about cash by FOCBS staff during a check, the person is obliged to report truthful information.
reviews.rationale: FOCBS information-on-request duty is supported with the trigger preserved: questioned about cash by FOCBS staff during a check. Actor normalization (you→person) does not change the proposition. Not a spontaneous declaration duty.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: If a person is, or is suspected of, carrying CHF 10,000 or more, FOCBS asks the person to disclose identity, the source of the cash, the intended use of the cash, and the beneficial owner.
reviews.rationale: FOCBS >= CHF 10,000 inquiry package supported. Operator 'CHF 10,000 or more' preserved; carrying-or-suspected-of-carrying trigger preserved; identity, source, intended use and beneficial owner categories preserved. Not a declaration threshold, permit, authorisation, or carriage ceiling. Operator conflict with page lead 'over 10,000' shorthand is resolved for this candidate by preferring the body 'or more' / ordinance 'mindestens' (>=) semantics.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: If the amount of cash equals or exceeds CHF 10,000, a respective entry is registered in the FOCBS information system.
reviews.rationale: FOCBS public information-system registration at equals-or-exceeds CHF 10,000 is supported as a recording/entry mechanic distinct from the CASH-004 inquiry package. Not characterized as statistical recording. Registration does not imply suspicion or prohibition. Keep distinct from Art. 6 amount-independent Meldung (CASH-013) for Adoption Gate.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Refusal to provide information or giving false information constitutes a customs offence and may result in a penalty.
reviews.rationale: FOCBS public-guidance consequence for refusal or false information is supported at customs-offence / may-result-in-penalty level. Does not establish automatic confiscation, permanent seizure, or a specific criminal conviction. Overlaps with statutory Art. 5 candidate CASH-012; duplication deferred to Adoption Gate.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: If there is any suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing, the cash may be seized temporarily and handed over to the police.
reviews.rationale: FOCBS temporary seizure and police handover on money-laundering or terrorist-financing suspicion is supported. Threshold-independent suspicion mechanism; does not establish that CHF 10,000+ cash is seized, nor permanent confiscation. Keep independent from Art. 4 provisional-seizure candidate CASH-011.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Im Sinne dieser Verordnung bedeuten Barmittel: Bargeld (schweizerische und ausländische Banknoten und Münzen, die als Zahlungsmittel im Umlauf sind) sowie übertragbare Inhaberpapiere, Aktien, Obligationen, Schecks und ähnliche Wertpapiere.
reviews.rationale: German Art. 2 Barmittel definition is supported. Declared compression omits lit. a (auskunftspflichtige Person) and restates lit. b categories including 'ähnliche Wertpapiere'. Do not silently equate to FOCBS public shorthand only. English publication rendering deferred to Adoption Gate / later translation review; M2.5 keeps German legal wording.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Die auskunftspflichtige Person muss im grenzüberschreitenden Verkehr auf ausdrückliche Befragung hin der Zollstelle Auskunft erteilen: a. zu ihrer Person; b. über die Ein-, Aus- und Durchfuhr von Barmitteln im Betrag von mindestens 10 000 Franken oder entsprechendem Gegenwert bei ausländischen Währungen; c. über die Herkunft und den vorgesehenen Verwendungszweck der Barmittel; d. über die wirtschaftlich berechtigte Person.
reviews.rationale: Art. 3 Abs. 1 express-questioning package is supported by direct restating of the German ordinance text. Operator 'mindestens 10 000 Franken' (>= CHF 10,000 / foreign-currency equivalent) preserved; Ein-/Aus-/Durchfuhr preserved; identity / origin / intended use / beneficial-owner categories preserved. Overlaps FOCBS CASH-004 public guidance but remains the statutory wording; do not flatten at M2.5. Not a spontaneous declaration duty.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Bei Verdacht auf Geldwäscherei oder Terrorismusfinanzierung kann die Zollstelle auch Auskünfte verlangen, wenn der Betrag der Barmittel den Schwellenwert von 10 000 Franken oder den entsprechenden Gegenwert bei ausländischen Währungen nicht erreicht.
reviews.rationale: Art. 3 Abs. 2 below-threshold suspicion information limb is supported. Customs may require information below CHF 10,000 where ML/TF suspicion exists. Prevents the false model that below CHF 10,000 is outside FOCBS information controls. Does not generalize to questioning for any reason, and does not by itself assert seizure or police referral.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Die Zollstelle kann nach Artikel 104 ZG Barmittel vorläufig beschlagnahmen; die vorläufige Beschlagnahme ist unabhängig vom Betrag der Barmittel zulässig.
reviews.rationale: Art. 4 provisional seizure under Art. 104 ZG is supported, including amount-independence. No CHF 10,000 trigger is imported. Provisional/vorläufig character preserved; not forfeiture. Independent from FOCBS CASH-007 public-guidance seizure surface for Adoption Gate.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Die verweigerte oder falsche Erteilung einer Auskunft nach Artikel 3 Absatz 1 Buchstaben a und b gilt als Ordnungswidrigkeit im Sinne von Artikel 127 Absatz 1 ZG.
reviews.rationale: Art. 5 is supported as a direct restatement limited to refused or false information under Art. 3 Abs. 1 lit. a and b (person; Ein-/Aus-/Durchfuhr of Barmittel at/above the threshold). Does not broaden to lit. c–d or to a generic border-cash non-compliance offence. Public-guidance CASH-006 remains a separate overlapping surface for Adoption Gate.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Die Meldung der Zollstellen an die Oberzolldirektion nach Artikel 6 ist unabhängig vom Betrag der Barmittel zulässig.
reviews.reviewed_text: Die Meldung ist unabhängig vom Betrag der Barmittel zulässig.
reviews.rationale: Bounded to restore exact Art. 6 Abs. 2 wording. Amount-independent Meldung permission is supported; do not attach a >= CHF 10,000 trigger. Meldung is authority reporting (Zollstellen → Oberzolldirektion per Art. 6 Abs. 1 context), not traveller cash declaration. Keep distinct from FOCBS public >=CHF10k information-system entry (CASH-005). Institutional destination detail from Abs. 1 is Adoption Gate composition, not forced into this Abs. 2 candidate.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: When establishing a business relationship, the financial intermediary must verify the identity of the customer on the basis of a document of evidentiary value.
reviews.rationale: AMLA Art. 3 para. 1 customer/contracting-party identity verification at business-relationship establishment is supported. Actor remains financial intermediary. Does not establish account entitlement for residents or non-residents, FCY-account rights, or FINMA/SNB prior approval.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: The financial intermediary must identify the beneficial owner with the due diligence required in the circumstances and verify its identity in order to ensure that it knows who the beneficial owner is.
reviews.rationale: AMLA Art. 4 para. 1 beneficial-owner identify+verify duty is supported. Special review: contracting party ≠ beneficial owner; listed-company exception remains in excerpt and is not erased. Does not prove account entitlement or that the account holder is necessarily the BO.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: If doubt arises in the course of the business relationship as to the identity of the customer or of the beneficial owner, the verification of identity or establishment of identity in terms of Articles 3 and 4 respectively must be repeated.
reviews.rationale: AMLA Art. 5 para. 1 repetition-on-doubt is supported with the statutory trigger preserved. Distinct from Art. 7 para. 1bis risk-based periodic record updating. Not annual or continuous re-identification of every client.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: The financial intermediary must clarify the economic background and the purpose of a transaction or of a business relationship if the transaction or business relationship appears unusual (unless its legality is clear), if there are relevant crime or terrorist-financing indications, if it carries a higher risk, or if customer/beneficial-owner/authorised-signatory data match or closely match data passed under Article 22a AMLA.
reviews.rationale: AMLA Art. 6 para. 2 special due-diligence clarification is supported with conditionality preserved (unusual / crime-or-TF indications / higher risk / Art. 22a data match). Special review: not every foreign customer, non-resident, FCY account, or cross-border transfer. Compressed lit. a–d triggers remain conditional.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: The financial intermediary must periodically check the required records to ensure that they are up to date, and update them if need be; the periodicity, scope and type of checking and updating are based on the risk posed by the customer.
reviews.rationale: AMLA Art. 7 para. 1bis risk-based periodic checking/updating of required records is supported. No fixed frequency invented. Ongoing diligence proposition — not an account-access prohibition and not continuous re-identification of all customers.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Banks must verify the identity of the contracting partner when establishing business relationships, including when opening accounts or passbooks and when opening securities accounts.
reviews.rationale: CDB 20 Art. 4 bank identity verification on establishing relationships, including opening accounts/passbooks and securities accounts, is supported. Actor remains bank (CDB scope) — not generalised to all financial intermediaries. KYC/onboarding ≠ legal entitlement to an account.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: If an operating legal entity or partnership has one or more controlling persons with voting rights or capital shares of 25% or more, these are to be identified in writing; a controlling person must generally be a natural person.
reviews.rationale: CDB 20 Art. 20 controlling-person identification for operating legal entities/partnerships (≥25% voting rights or capital shares; generally natural person) is supported. Controlling person ≠ beneficial owner of every account asset. 25% mechanic is CDB Art. 20 scope — not universalised across all AML contexts.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: For natural persons, banks must appropriately document name, first name, date of birth, nationality and the actual domicile address as well as the means used to prove identity.
reviews.rationale: CDB 20 Art. 7 para. 1 natural-person documentation (including actual domicile address) is supported as an identification/data requirement. Does not create a Swiss statutory resident/non-resident account category, residence-based entitlement, or foreign-resident ban.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Business relationships and transactions with heightened risk, such as business relationships with clients in high-risk countries or with politically exposed persons (PEPs), must be recorded and clarified in greater detail.
reviews.rationale: FINMA supervisory heightened-risk recording/clarification is supported. Examples (high-risk countries / PEPs) illustrate heightened risk — they do not redefine all non-residents or all foreign domiciles as high-risk. Country risk ≠ residency class. Special review addressed.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Boards of directors of financial intermediaries must establish a clearly defined money-laundering risk tolerance, including clear communications regarding particularly high-risk clients, high-risk countries and services that are deemed outside the risk tolerance limits.
reviews.rationale: FINMA risk-tolerance / outside-tolerance supervisory expectation is supported as an institutional acceptance boundary (boards define risk tolerance; certain high-risk clients/countries/services may be outside limits). Not a statutory ban, FINMA approval requirement, residency-specific prohibition, or governmental account-opening licence. Useful later against legacy 'freely' — but not a national access rule at M2.5.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: For high-risk client relationships of the kind addressed by FINMA, the origin of the client's assets must be clarified in detail and verified as originating from legal sources, and higher-risk transactions must be monitored very carefully.
reviews.rationale: FINMA high-risk source-of-assets clarification and careful higher-risk transaction monitoring are supported within the high-risk client relationships context addressed by the source page. Not universal: foreign customers / all non-residents must prove source of wealth. Special review addressed.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: The bank requires from its contracting partner a statement concerning the beneficial ownership of the assets when opening accounts or passbooks and when opening securities accounts.
reviews.rationale: CDB 20 Art. 27 bank requirement of a beneficial-ownership statement when opening accounts/passbooks and securities accounts is supported. Bank/CDB actor preserved. Contracting party ≠ beneficial owner. Does not establish account entitlement. CDB chapter-4 exceptions remain for Adoption Gate scope discipline and are not erased by supporting the core opening duty.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: The revised Anti-Money Laundering Act and the new Act on the Transparency of Legal Persons and the Identification of Beneficial Owners will enter into force on 1 October 2026.
reviews.rationale: Federal Council announcement that the revised AMLA and the Act on the Transparency of Legal Persons / beneficial owners enter into force on 1 October 2026 is supported as a temporal/future proposition (scope.temporal_scope=effective_from). On 2026-09-09 the reform is not current operative law. Must not support current Switzerland drafting. Special temporal review addressed.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: On 12 May 2026, FINMA launched the consultation on the partially revised AMLO-FINMA; the consultation ran until 9 June 2026 and is not itself the current operative ordinance.
reviews.rationale: FINMA AMLO-FINMA partial-revision consultation launched 12 May 2026 (to 9 June 2026) is supported as a process/consultation fact. Explicit boundary that the consultation is not the current operative ordinance is retained and correct. Not transformed into adopted/final regulation or into current AMLO-FINMA text. Special temporal review addressed.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: If a business relationship or transaction appears unusual or if there are indications that the funds stem from criminal activity or serve to finance terrorism, the financial intermediary must clarify the financial background and purpose of the business relationship or transaction.
reviews.rationale: FINMA supervisory restatement of conditional clarification (unusual relationship/transaction or crime/TF fund indications) is supported as current supervisory guidance. Overlaps AMLA Art. 6 for Adoption Gate reconciliation — not a M2.5 defect. Does not broaden Art. 6 into universal foreign-client SoF. AML clarification ≠ exchange control.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Pecuniary debts must be discharged in legal tender of the currency in which the debt was incurred.
reviews.rationale: CO Art. 84 para. 1 pecuniary-debt currency-of-discharge proposition is supported verbatim from Fedlex. Contractual monetary-obligation mechanics only. Does not establish universal FCY invoicing freedom, unrestricted FX conversion, cross-border settlement entitlement, capital-movement rights, or bank-execution guarantees.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: A debt expressed in a currency other than the national currency of the place of payment may be discharged in that national currency at the rate of exchange that applies on the day it falls due.
reviews.rationale: CO Art. 84 para. 2 local-currency substitution limb is supported. Debtor may discharge a non-local-currency debt in the national currency of the place of payment at the maturity exchange rate. Special review: literal-performance exception intentionally omitted here and retained in CC-CH-BIZ-003. Does not imply mandatory CHF payment, universal invoicing freedom, or unrestricted FX/capital rights.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Literal performance in the stipulated currency is required where the contract includes the expression 'actual currency' or words to that effect, excluding the debtor's option to discharge a non-local-currency debt in the national currency of the place of payment.
reviews.rationale: CO Art. 84 para. 2 'actual currency' / words-to-that-effect literal-performance exception is supported (official EN; DE 'effektiv'). Special review addressed: exception excludes the Art. 84 para. 2 substitution option. Does not invent mandatory FCY performance absent the contractual qualification, nor transfer/invoicing freedom.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: For purposes of calculating the VAT payable, considerations paid in foreign currency must be converted into national currency at the date the tax claim arises.
reviews.rationale: VAT Ordinance Art. 45 para. 1 FCY-consideration conversion into national currency for VAT calculation at the tax-claim date is supported. Special review: tax conversion ≠ requirement that the underlying commercial obligation or settlement be denominated or paid in CHF. Does not create a universal contractual invoice-currency rule.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: A consideration is in foreign currency if the invoice or the receipt is issued in foreign currency; it is irrelevant whether the payment is in national or foreign currency.
reviews.rationale: VAT Ordinance Art. 45 para. 2 definition is supported: a consideration is in foreign currency if the invoice/receipt is issued in foreign currency, and payment currency is irrelevant for that classification. Special review: this is a VAT assessment definition, not evidence of a universal federal commercial right to invoice in any currency. CH-H3-MISSING-UNIVERSAL-INVOICE-CURRENCY-RULE remains not established.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Considerations in foreign currency need to be converted into Swiss francs for the purposes of calculating the domestic tax and the reverse charge at the time the tax claim arises, using either the monthly average rate published by the Federal Tax Administration FTA or the daily exchange rate (sell).
reviews.rationale: FTA VAT FX guidance is supported for converting FCY considerations into CHF for domestic tax and reverse-charge calculation using FTA monthly average or daily sell rates. Special review: methodology/date for VAT assessment only — not a contractual settlement prohibition and not a mandatory bank customer FX rate.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Accounting is carried out in the national currency or in the currency required for business operations.
reviews.rationale: CO Art. 957a para. 4 accounting-currency rule is supported: national currency or currency required for business operations. Bookkeeping currency only. Does not create invoice, payment, transfer, or bank-account currency rights.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Financial reports are presented in the national currency or in the currency required for business operations; if the national currency is not used, the values must also be shown in the national currency and the exchange rates applied must be published in the notes to the accounts.
reviews.rationale: CO Art. 958d para. 3 financial-reporting currency presentation is supported, including dual national-currency figures and exchange-rate disclosure when not using national currency. Reporting presentation ≠ payment or transfer entitlement.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: The Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) payment system is Switzerland's central payment system, operated by SIX Interbank Clearing Ltd on behalf of the Swiss National Bank; eligible participants primarily include Swiss banks and other financial market participants, and SIC processes large-value transactions as well as retail payments connected with services provided by financial market participants (bank transfers, card payments, direct debits).
reviews.rationale: SNB SIC infrastructure description is supported: Switzerland's central payment system, operated by SIX Interbank Clearing Ltd on behalf of the SNB; participants primarily Swiss banks and other financial market participants; large-value and retail payments (bank transfers, card payments, direct debits). Special review: infrastructure ≠ universal customer payment entitlement, unrestricted FX, unrestricted cross-border transfer, capital-movement freedom, or SNB per-payment approval.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Instant payments allow private individuals and companies to settle domestic account-to-account transactions with immediate execution and final settlement in seconds, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week (including public holidays).
reviews.rationale: SNB domestic instant-payment description is supported: domestic account-to-account transactions with immediate execution and final settlement in seconds, 24/7 including public holidays. Domestic only. Does not establish cross-currency or cross-border instant production capability.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: The Swiss National Bank and the European Central Bank are conducting an exploration phase throughout 2026 to evaluate an interlinking between the SIC instant payment service and the Eurosystem's TIPS service; the exploration assesses feasibility and economic viability and does not itself establish operational cross-currency instant settlement.
reviews.rationale: SNB 29 September 2025 press release is supported as a temporal/exploration proposition: SNB–ECB exploration throughout 2026 of SIC IP–TIPS interlinking for feasibility and economic viability. Special temporal review addressed (CH-SRC-CONFLICT-IP-DOMESTIC-VS-EXPLORATION). Exploration ≠ operational cross-currency instant settlement. Must not support current drafting as if interlinking were in production.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Under applicable sanctions ordinances, financial intermediaries are required to implement the prohibitions, freeze the assets of sanctioned persons, and report affected business relationships to SECO; a report to SECO does not relieve the intermediary of AMLA clarification and MROS reporting duties where suspicion remains.
reviews.reviewed_text: Under the applicable Ukraine sanctions ordinance as notified by FINMA on 7 April 2026, financial intermediaries are called upon to implement the prohibitions, freeze the assets of sanctioned persons, and report affected business relationships to SECO; a report to SECO does not relieve the intermediary of additional clarifications under AMLA Art. 6 where suspicion remains, nor of an immediate MROS report under AMLA Art. 9 where those clarifications cannot be dispelled.
reviews.rationale: Bounded for source-scope fidelity. Captured authority is the FINMA 7 April 2026 Ukraine sanctions-update notice (German verbatim). The operative FI duties — implement prohibitions, freeze sanctioned persons' assets, report affected relationships to SECO, and non-displacement of AMLA Art. 6/9 — are supported for that ordinance pathway. Special review: do not generalise this notice into a universal statement about every Swiss sanctions regime without additional authorities. Sanctions mechanism ≠ routine payment approval and ≠ displacement of the H2 AML framework.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: On 19 December 2025, Parliament adopted the Investment Screening Act, which aims to subject acquisitions of Swiss companies operating in especially critical sectors by foreign state-controlled investors to prior approval; entry into force is expected in 2027.
reviews.rationale: SECO Investment Screening page is supported as a temporal/future proposition: Parliament adopted the ISA on 19 December 2025; prior approval targets acquisitions of Swiss companies in especially critical sectors by foreign state-controlled investors; entry into force expected in 2027. Special temporal review addressed (CH-SRC-CONFLICT-ISA-TEMPORAL-2027). Not current ordinary FX/payment/capital-remittance approval on 2026-09-10.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: As the Investment Screening Act is expected to enter into force only in 2027, no applications can currently be submitted or reviewed.
reviews.rationale: SECO statement that ISA applications cannot currently be submitted or reviewed because entry into force is expected only in 2027 is supported as a current non-operability fact on 2026-09-10. Special review: confirms ISA is not an available current approval pathway for ordinary payments/FX/transfers. Complements CC-CH-BIZ-013 temporal boundary.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: The de jure exchange-rate arrangement for Switzerland is free floating.
reviews.rationale: IMF 2026 Article IV Informational Annex Exchange Rate Arrangement states verbatim that the de jure exchange-rate arrangement is free floating. Supported as an IMF de jure classification only. Special review: does not establish absence of intervention, exchange controls, capital restrictions, de facto floating, unrestricted payments, or full liberalisation. Coexists with REG-004 de facto crawl-like classification.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: The exchange rate of the Swiss franc is determined by market forces in the foreign exchange market, and all settlements are made at free-market rates.
reviews.reviewed_text: Under the IMF 2026 Article IV Informational Annex exchange-rate arrangement statement, the exchange rate of the Swiss franc is determined by market forces in the foreign exchange market, and all settlements are made at free-market rates.
reviews.rationale: Bounded to pin the IMF Informational Annex exchange-rate-arrangement / exchange-system context. Source sentence is supported, but 'all settlements' / free-market rates must not be read as retail mid-market pricing, zero spreads/fees, no SNB intervention, or unrestricted capital/payments. Special review: market-rate formation ≠ customer dealing price.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: The Swiss National Bank reserves the right to intervene in the foreign exchange market.
reviews.rationale: IMF 2026 Informational Annex states the SNB reserves the right to intervene in the foreign exchange market. Supported as institutional capability/right only. Special review: not continuous intervention, not an exchange-rate target/peg/crawl/managed float, not customer transaction approval, and not an exchange-control regime.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: The de facto exchange-rate arrangement is classified as crawl-like from 25 April 2025, as bilateral volatility of the exchange rate against the euro has been below the 2-percent threshold.
reviews.rationale: IMF 2026 Informational Annex classifies the de facto exchange-rate arrangement as crawl-like from 25 April 2025 because bilateral EUR volatility has been below the 2-percent threshold. Supported as IMF statistical/de facto taxonomy only. Special review: do not normalise crawl-like into crawling peg, managed float, target corridor, or formal crawling mechanism; does not collapse or contradict REG-001 de jure free floating.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Switzerland has accepted the obligations of Article VIII, Sections 2, 3, and 4 of the IMF’s Articles of Agreement.
reviews.rationale: IMF 2026 Informational Annex states Switzerland has accepted Article VIII Sections 2, 3, and 4. Supported as international-law acceptance posture only. Special review: not capital-account liberalisation, not absence of sanctions, not a private transfer right, and not absence of prudential/OECD reservations.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Switzerland maintains an exchange system that is free of multiple currency practices and of restrictions on the making of payments and transfers for current international transactions, except for restrictions in place for security reasons notified to the IMF pursuant to Executive Board Decision No. 144–(52/51).
reviews.rationale: IMF 2026 Informational Annex exchange-system sentence supports every limb: free of multiple currency practices; free of restrictions on payments and transfers for CURRENT international transactions; except security restrictions notified under Executive Board Decision No. 144–(52/51). Exception preserved. Special review: not all payments unrestricted; not capital unrestricted; not no exchange controls generally; not no sanctions; not bank-client transfer entitlement. Distinct from OECD capital reservations (REG-013..017).

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: In order to fulfil its monetary-policy mandate, the SNB may purchase and sell foreign currency against Swiss francs on the financial markets.
reviews.rationale: SNB Implementation of monetary policy page states the SNB may purchase and sell foreign currency against Swiss francs to fulfil its monetary-policy mandate. Supported for SNB actor and monetary-policy purpose only. Special review: not resident free FX entitlement, not bank conversion duty, not customer rate-setting, and not exchange-control characterisation of intervention.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Foreign-exchange transactions conducted by the SNB are usually spot or swap transactions.
reviews.rationale: SNB Implementation page states foreign-exchange transactions conducted by the SNB are usually spot or swap transactions. Supported as SNB institutional mechanics only. Special review: not a statement about all Swiss FX transactions, retail products, capital-movement rules, or customer conversion availability.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: The SNB can conclude foreign-exchange transactions with a wide range of domestic and foreign counterparties.
reviews.rationale: SNB Implementation page states the SNB can conclude FX transactions with a wide range of domestic and foreign counterparties. Supported as SNB counterparty-policy scope only. Special review: not universal entitlement for any person to trade with SNB and not unrestricted cross-border capital flows.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: As of the SNB monetary-policy assessment of 18 June 2026, if necessary the SNB has an increased willingness to intervene in the foreign-exchange market to counter a rapid and excessive appreciation of the Swiss franc that would jeopardise price stability in Switzerland.
reviews.rationale: SNB Monetary Policy Assessment of 18 June 2026 states that if necessary the SNB has an increased willingness to intervene in the foreign-exchange market to counter rapid and excessive CHF appreciation that would jeopardise price stability. Supported as temporal policy posture pinned to that assessment. Special review: not proof of continuous or current intervention volume; not an exchange-rate target/peg/cap; not managed float; not the cause of the IMF crawl-like classification.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Since 1 January 2003, the Federal Act on the Implementation of International Sanctions (Embargo Act / Embargogesetz, EmbG) has been the legal basis for Switzerland’s implementation of sanctions measures; the Embargo Act is a framework law, and the concrete sanctions measures are contained in separate ordinances based on that Act.
reviews.rationale: SECO legal-basis page supports Embargo Act (EmbG) as the framework legal basis for Swiss sanctions implementation since 1 January 2003, with concrete measures in separate ordinances based on the Act. Supported as domestic legal architecture. Special review: EmbG framework ≠ every asset frozen; ≠ every payment restricted; ≠ every sanctions measure is an IMF-notified exchange restriction.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Under the Embargo Act, the Federal Council is empowered to enact coercive measures such as financial sanctions, trade restrictions, travel bans, or the freezing of assets.
reviews.rationale: SECO general sanctions page states the Embargo Act empowers the Federal Council to enact coercive measures such as financial sanctions, trade restrictions, travel bans, or asset freezes. Supported as FC capability/framework vocabulary. Special review: 'such as' categories are illustrative of powers, not proof every measure is currently imposed in every regime; not customer Federal Council approval for ordinary transfers; not general capital-transfer controls.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Under the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements, Switzerland maintains a List A I/A reservation on inward direct investment by non-residents limited to specified sectors and situations, including film distribution/exhibition companies, certain real-estate acquisitions requiring cantonal authorisation when not used for a permanent establishment, Rhine/maritime ship registration, aircraft registration and majority-Swiss-controlled airline investment (subject to international agreements), hydroelectricity / oil and gas pipelines / nuclear energy, and broadcasting foreign ownership above 49 percent.
reviews.rationale: OECD Annex B Switzerland List A I/A reservation on inward direct investment by non-residents is limited to the enumerated sectors/situations restated in the candidate. Supported as a bounded OECD reservation, not a universal FDI approval regime. Special review: not general foreign-investment ban; not FX-conversion approval; not capital-transfer licence; reservation ≠ general prohibition.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Under the OECD Code Annex B, Switzerland maintains a List B III reservation under which acquisition of real estate in Switzerland by non-residents is subject to cantonal authorisation when the acquirer does not use the property to operate a permanent establishment; holiday-home authorisations are subject to quotas; and real-estate investments of a purely financial nature are not permitted, with some exceptions.
reviews.rationale: OECD Annex B List B III non-resident real-estate reservation is supported: cantonal authorisation when property is not used to operate a permanent establishment; holiday-home quotas; purely financial real-estate investments not permitted with some exceptions. Special review: not all non-resident property requires authorisation in every case; not FX/payment-transfer approval; not all inbound capital transfers require approval.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Under the OECD Code Annex B List A IV/D1 reservation, purchases abroad by residents of specified non-resident-issued securities are reserved where those assets would exceed stated percentage limits of private pension-fund liability-representative assets or insurance technical-reserve cover, and pension funds must also operate within an overall 30 percent limit of total foreign assets allowed as part of mandatory reserves.
reviews.rationale: OECD Annex B List A IV/D1 reservation on purchase abroad of specified non-resident-issued securities by private pension funds / insurance companies, including the overall 30% foreign-asset limit for pension mandatory reserves, is supported. Special review: institutional prudential reservation only — not a household 30% foreign-investment limit; not a general company capital control; not a general foreign-securities prohibition.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Under the OECD Code Annex B List B V/D1 reservation, purchases of money-market securities abroad by residents are reserved where non-resident-issued debt instruments would exceed 30 percent of private pension-fund liability-representative assets (subject also to the overall 30 percent foreign-asset limit) or, for insurance technical-reserve cover, where such instruments are not securitised/quoted/regularly traded on an active market.
reviews.rationale: OECD Annex B List B V/D1 money-market purchase-abroad reservation for private pension funds / insurance companies is supported with the stated percentage and quality/active-market conditions and overall pension foreign-asset interaction. Special review: not a general resident money-market capital control.

reviews.candidate_text_snapshot: Under the OECD Code Annex B List B XI/B1 and B2 reservation, operation of deposit accounts by residents with non-resident institutions in domestic or foreign currency is reserved where such deposits would exceed 30 percent of private pension-fund liability-representative assets (subject also to the overall 30 percent foreign-asset limit) or would cover insurance technical reserves where the priority privilege of those assets under Swiss regulation cannot be granted.
reviews.reviewed_text: Under the OECD Code Annex B List B XI/B1 and B2 reservation, deposits of funds by private pension funds or insurance companies with non-resident financial institutions in domestic or foreign currency are reserved where such deposits would exceed 30 percent of private pension-fund liability-representative assets (subject also to the overall 30 percent foreign-asset limit for pension mandatory reserves) or would cover insurance technical reserves where the priority privilege of those assets under Swiss regulation cannot be granted.
reviews.rationale: Bounded to front-load institutional actors. Candidate_text leads with 'operation of deposit accounts by residents…' before the pension/insurance remark conditions and is prone to overreading as a universal resident offshore-deposit restriction. OECD remark limits the reservation to private pension funds and insurance technical-reserve covers. Special review: not a general ban on Swiss residents holding foreign bank accounts; not a universal 30% offshore-deposit limit; not government approval for all foreign deposits.
